q: West Bromwich Albion were formed in 1878 by workers from George Salter's Spring Works. Under what name did the club play before adopting 'Albion' in 1880?
hint: The factory men who founded the club called themselves the Strollers. The 'Albion' suffix arrived in 1880, and Albion were the first English club to take it.

q: In which year did Albion move into The Hawthorns?
hint: The first match at the new ground was a 1-1 draw with Derby County in September 1900, and Albion have never moved since.

q: Which bird appears on Albion's club badge, perched on a branch?
hint: The song thrush, known locally as a throstle, gave Albion one of their oldest nicknames — the Throstles — and it sits on a sprig of hawthorn.

q: Jeff Astle's extra-time goal won the 1968 FA Cup final for Albion. Which club did they beat at Wembley?
hint: Astle struck three minutes into extra time to settle it 1-0 against Everton, completing a run in which he had scored in every round of the competition.

q: Cyrille Regis, Laurie Cunningham and Brendon Batson were known collectively by which nickname during their time together at Albion?
hint: The trio were named after the American vocal group, and were among the first black players to line up together in a First Division side.

q: Laurie Cunningham left Albion in 1979 for which club, becoming the first British player to sign for them?
hint: Real Madrid paid a club-record fee in pesetas for the winger in July 1979, and he scored twice on his debut.

q: Albion won the 1892 FA Cup final 3-0. Which Midlands club did they beat?
hint: A one-sided derby win over Aston Villa gave Albion their second FA Cup, after the 1888 victory over Preston North End.

q: In 1930-31 Albion completed a double no English club has managed before or since: the FA Cup plus what?
hint: Albion went up from the Second Division and beat Birmingham 2-1 at Wembley in the same season, W. G. Richardson scoring both goals in the final.

q: Albion have been champions of England once. In which season?
hint: In the first season after the First World War Albion took the title with 104 goals and 60 points, both league records at the time.

q: In the season Albion won the 1954 FA Cup they also finished league runners-up. Which club took the title ahead of them?
hint: Wolves won their first championship in 1953-54, denying Vic Buckingham's side the League and Cup double.

q: Albion's only League Cup triumph came in 1966, in the last final played over two legs. Who did they beat 5-3 on aggregate?
hint: West Ham won the first leg 2-1 in London before Albion hit four at The Hawthorns; a year later Albion lost the first Wembley League Cup final to QPR.

q: Ron Atkinson signed Brendon Batson for Albion in 1978 from the club he had himself just left as manager. Which club?
hint: Atkinson had taken Cambridge United out of the Fourth Division before moving to The Hawthorns in January 1978, and brought Batson with him.

q: Which player holds Albion's club records for both most appearances and most goals?
hint: 'Bomber' Brown played 720 games and scored 279 goals between 1963 and 1980, and finished 1970-71 as the First Division's top scorer from midfield.

q: Which Albion player was sent home from the 1978 World Cup finals after failing a drugs test?
hint: Johnston tested positive after Scotland's defeat by Peru in Argentina, was banned from international football, and soon left The Hawthorns for Vancouver.

q: On 30 December 1978 Albion won 5-3 away from home in a match still rated among English football's greatest. At which ground?
hint: It was 3-3 at half-time at Old Trafford before Albion pulled away; Len Cantello's volley was voted goal of the season.

q: As holders of the FA Cup, Albion entered the 1968-69 European Cup Winners' Cup and went out in the quarter-finals to which club?
hint: A goalless draw in Scotland was followed by a 1-0 Dunfermline win at The Hawthorns, and the Scots went on to reach the semi-finals.

q: Albion signed Cyrille Regis in 1977 from which non-League club?
hint: Regis was playing for Hayes when Albion paid an initial £5,000, with a further sum due after 20 appearances — one of the great bargains of the era.

q: Manchester United paid a then British record fee to sign Bryan Robson from Albion in October 1981. How much was it?
hint: The £1.5m deal reunited Robson with Ron Atkinson, who had left The Hawthorns for Old Trafford a few months earlier.

q: Albion signed Jeff Astle in 1964 from which club?
hint: Astle stepped up from Notts County to the First Division with Albion, and supporters came to know him simply as 'The King'.

q: Which ground did Albion leave when they moved to The Hawthorns in 1900?
hint: Stoney Lane was Albion's home from 1885 to 1900, covering their first two FA Cup wins; the club's earlier grounds were all short stays.
